name: The Star
upright: A BIA that knows what must return first and how fast, backups that truly restore, and a plan rehearsed until it works.
reversed: A plan never tested, backups never restored, an RTO longer than the business can survive: hope mistaken for recovery.
vision: A kneeling figure keeps one foot on land and one in a pool. From one jug they refill the pool, where a tide mark shows the most water that may be lost. From the other they water the land as two hourglasses run end to end, racing a sundial's shadow to a red line. Five streams fan out, each wider than the last: the first only dampens a written page, the last drowns the old riverbed. Overhead, seven small stars copy the great one: the first takes all its light, each later one only what changed since the last. In the tree an ibis keeps three nests: one full of eggs, one of straw, one of bare twigs.
decode: The pool's tide mark → RPO: the most data you can afford to lose, measured in time; it sets how often you back up.
Two hourglasses racing the sundial's red line → RTO plus WRT must fit inside the MTD; a recovery slower than the MTD fails the business.
Five streams, from a dampened page to a drowned riverbed → DR tests from least to most disruptive: read-through, walk-through, simulation, parallel, full interruption.
Seven stars, the first with all the light, the rest only what changed → a full backup plus incrementals: restoring needs the full and every incremental since, in order.
Nests of eggs, of straw, of bare twigs → hot site (ready, current data), warm site (equipment but no current data), cold site (space and power only).
facts: Differential backups copy everything changed since the last full and leave the archive bit set, so a restore needs only the full plus the latest differential.
Return from the alternate site with the least critical functions first, so the repaired primary site proves itself before critical work moves back.
RAID and clustering are fault tolerance, not backup: RAID 1 mirrors; RAID 5 stripes with parity across at least three disks and survives one disk failure.
trap: The collective keeps swapping RTO and RPO. RTO is how fast a system must be back, and it must be shorter than the MTD; RPO is how much data may be lost, counted back to the last good backup.
